subject: Discovery postmortem: SDK adapter recommendations & pilot readiness
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Margo Lee <margo@neurolytics.ai>, Alex Browne <alex.browne@neurolytics.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery postmortem: SDK adapter recommendations & pilot readiness

Hi Margo / Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick post-call summary and concrete next steps so we’re all aligned.

Top pain points you shared
- Latency spikes on multi-turn clinical summarization (~600–1k tokens) are causing friction for triage workflows.
- Cost sensitivity for live clinician-facing features — budget target is ~40% lower per-session than current baseline.
- Regulatory/data controls: all PHI must remain in your VPC during the pilot, and audit logs must be retained 90 days.

Goals we agreed
1) Pilot a constrained production flow for triage summarization (~500 requests/day) with streaming responses for progressive UI.
2) Deliver an SDK adapter that maps your existing call patterns (conversation + chart context) into Redwood function-calling + structured JSON output for downstream EHR ingestion.
3) Measure latency, tokens-per-session, and quality (clinician-rated summary accuracy) over a 4-week window.

High-level technical approach (proposed)
- Use our private deployment in your AWS account (VPC peering) for PHI controls.
- SDK adapter: small shim that will convert your request envelope to Redwood Generate + function-calling for structured sections (history, assessment, plan).
- Streaming: enable incremental tokens with a fallback to non-streaming for long tails; core path will target 200–400ms per token when possible.
- Embeddings + rerank: precompute candidate context vectors (512-d) and select top-K for summarization to reduce prompt length and cost.

Immediate asks / next steps
- From Neurolytics: sample anonymized session payloads (1–3 examples, with PHI replaced) and a short rubric you’ll use for clinical quality (due Thu EOD).
- From Redwood: draft SDK adapter spec, proposed function schema, and SLA draft (attached).
- Schedule: pilot kickoff next Tue 11am PT to align infra & access.

Attachments: neurolytics-requirements-outline.pdf, redwood-sla-draft-v1.pdf

I’ll follow up with an internal task list and owners. Thanks — Ben

--
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery postmortem: SDK adapter recommendations & pilot readiness

Thanks Ben — this lines up with our notes. A couple clarifications: 

- Sample payloads: we’ll scrub PHI and send 2 representative sessions by Thursday. One is a short triage (200 tokens), the other is a problem-focused consult (900 tokens) to test the long-tail behavior.
- Regarding embeddings: we use a semantic similarity reranking currently with an internal 768-d model; happy to try Redwood embeddings if you recommend 512-d for latency/cost tradeoffs.
- Security: VPC peering + KMS integration is a hard requirement; we cannot allow any hosted token exchange.

We confirm the kickoff for Tue 11am PT — Alex and our platform lead (Margo) will be there. Looking forward to the SDK spec.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Neurolytics pilot — SDK adapter & infra owners (short tasks)

Marissa / Sergio — quick internal checklist to prep for the Tue kickoff. No external recipients on this note.

Context: Neurolytics needs an SDK adapter + function schema for structured output (history/assessment/plan), streaming-enabled responses with a fallback path, and embeddings-based rerank. They will require VPC peering and KMS integration for the pilot.

Immediate items (owners):
- Marissa: draft SDK adapter interface (JS + Python examples), include a small shim that converts their existing request envelope -> Redwood Generate + function-calling. Deliverable: PR with examples by Fri EOD.
- Sergio: infra checklist for private deployment in their account (VPC peering steps, KMS key exchange, audit log retention 90 days). Also prepare a runbook for switching streaming on/off per-route. Deliverable: infra checklist doc by Mon noon.
- Ben (me): finalize function schema (JSON schema for sections), initial latency/cost target matrix, and the pilot acceptance criteria doc. Deliverable: send to Neurolytics Thu AM.

Technical notes to include in the SDK spec:
- Function calling: explicit typed output for fields: {"summary":"string","diagnosis":{"codes":[]},"plan":{"actions":[]}} to avoid downstream parsing errors.
- Streaming behavior: chunked token stream with message-level checkpoints (every ~250 tokens) and a final consolidation call that writes the structured object.
- Embeddings: recommend 512-d candidate vectors for faster nearest-neighbor and lower storage; propose hybrid rerank (coarse 512-d ANN -> fine-grained scorer).
- Quality: include a small eval harness (5 prompts) that we can run nightly to detect regressions during the pilot.

I’ll draft the SDK spec and SLA and attach them to the outbound message. Flag any blockers here.

Thanks,
Ben

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 18:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Mutual action plan & pilot kickoff — files attached

Hi Margo / Alex — attaching the SDK adapter spec and SLA draft per our plan. Summary of the mutual action plan below; please confirm owners and the sample payload delivery.

Mutual action plan (high level)
- Thu (5/6) — Neurolytics: provide 2 sample anonymized sessions + clinical quality rubric.
- Fri (5/7) — Redwood: deliver SDK adapter spec (JS/Python examples), function schema, and initial test harness.
- Mon (5/10) — Infra finalization: VPC peering + KMS handshake completed (Sergio + Neurolytics infra lead).
- Tue (5/11) 11am PT — Pilot kickoff meeting (agenda: access, test data, success metrics).
- Week of 5/17 — Pilot begins; 4-week measurement window starts.

Acceptance criteria for pilot start
- SDK adapter can call Redwood Generate with function-calling and return valid structured JSON for 90% of test cases in the rubric.
- Streaming path returns incremental tokens within target 200–400ms/token for median cases.
- Embedding-retrieval path reduces tokens-per-session by at least 30% vs baseline.

Attachments: neurolytics-requirements-outline.pdf, redwood-sla-draft-v1.pdf

Please reply with confirmations and let us know if any timeline items are infeasible.

Thanks — Ben
